General
* To avoid confusion, please avoid the term / variable name "turns" and use "rounds" instead, as "turn" may be interpreted as a rotation. Consider describing the puzzle as consisting of a number of rounds, and in each round the seats undergo the specified number of 90° rotations.

* Would it be possible to rewrite the narrative to make the simulation more realistic and easier to understand? While rotating seats is acceptable as a whimsical idea, I can't picture seats and fans overlapping, let alone rival fans somehow disappearing.

  Instead of physically moving seats, perhaps use concepts such as banners, spotlights, light beams, or chanting, where opposing elements cancel out, single or matching elements remain (or reinforce each other), and empty spaces contribute nothing.

* At the moment, I don't fully understand the simulation, and I'm trying not to look at the solution. A more intuitive and believable scenario would make it much easier for reviewers to understand the intended behaviour and provide further feedback.

Goal
* Please change the example to use one positive integer greater than +1 and one negative integer less than -1 to better demonstrate multiple rotations within a round.

* The example should clearly explain how the intermediate state after each round of rotations is obtained.

Input
* Line 1 & Line 2:
  • Please add "odd" before "integer".

  • Please replace "grid" with "stadium's seating plan".

* Line 4:

  • Please change "An array of" to "[[n]] non-zero".

  • Please correct the typo: seperated => separated.

  • Please specify that every integer is preceded by either {{+}} or {{-}} to indicate the direction of a rotation.

Output
* Please change "Line" to "line".

Constraints
* Please remove both existing constraints.

* Please add a constraint for each of h, w, n and (each integer in) turns.

Stub generator
* Please rewrite Line 4 using loopline.

* Please add a write statement.

Cases
* Test 4: w is 24, not 25.

* Each test-validator pair should avoid mixing cases where [[h]] > [[w]] and [[h]] < [[w]].

* Please add a pair of cases where [[h]] = [[w]].

* I'll provide more feedback on the cases after I understand the puzzle better.

Cover picture
* Please upload a cover picture for the puzzle (this can wait until the puzzle concept and narrative have been clarified).

Thanks.

You're right—the original story was something I put together quickly without giving much thought to whether it actually justified the mechanics of the puzzle. After quite a bit of deliberation, I've now rewritten the narrative from scratch around a completely different concept that better explains the simulation.

For the test cases, I initially generated them rather randomly while developing the puzzle. I haven't started refining them yet, so I'll revisit them after the statement and overall concept are finalized. At that stage, I'll also address the feedback regarding the validators, additional case pairs, and the other test case improvements you've suggested.

Thanks.

+
About the Stub generator, loopline n turn:int is showing error because of '+', and can't read it in string form also ("stubGenerator.StringInLoopLine")

Goal
* The statement says there are "three states", but then immediately introduces three characters (A, B, whitespace), three channels (Channel A, Channel B, Open Channel), and their behaviour. Consider introducing them more directly. For example, state that each position on a strip is one of the three channels, represented by the corresponding characters. This avoids describing the same concept using multiple terms.

* Please specify the initial orientation of the front-center strip.

* Consider replacing "is permanently fixed" with "never rotates" to make it clear what's fixed.

* Consider formatting the first instance of "diagnostic bus" in <<bold>>, as it's a key term.

* The statement says

> The center horizontal strip… serves as the matrix's diagnostic bus.

> …it overlaps the diagnostic bus, and the states of the two strips combine…

However, it never explicitly explains what happens to the diagnostic bus after the combination. Consider avoiding describing the center horizontal strip as the diagnostic bus, which mixes the concepts of "strip" and "diagnostic bus". Instead, simply mention that the diagnostic bus is formed by the combined states of the two strips, or by the horizontal strip alone when the front-center strip is vertical.

* The statement doesn't explain what happens when the front-center strip is vertical. This ambiguity would naturally be resolved by clarifying how the diagnostic bus is determined, as suggested above.

* The explanation of the routing rules feels unnecessarily complicated. The lookup table already defines the behaviour unambiguously, so introducing the terms "complementary" and "incompatible" adds flavour without improving understanding.

* From the states:
  • Channel A allows type-A signals.
  • Channel B allows type-B signals.
  • Open Channel allows both types of signals.

  It follows that:
  • A+A / B+B => still allows type-A / type-B only
  • A+B or B+A => allows both types.

  These two interpretations appear contradictory, as the Open Channel should allow both types of signals:
  • A+Open or Open+A => A only???
  • B+Open or Open+B => B only???

* The description of the rotation values could be clearer. The phrase "90° clockwise per unit" is awkward, as the statement never defines what a "unit" is. Consider instead stating that a positive value indicates the number of 90° clockwise rotations, while a negative value indicates the number of 90° counterclockwise rotations.

* The wording "If the rotated strip extends beyond the diagnostic bus, output the additional cells" is vague. Consider stating explicitly that overlapping positions are combined according to the routing rules, while non-overlapping positions retain the state of the longer strip.

* The rules about the matrix not resetting between maintenance rounds and handling strips of different lengths would fit more naturally immediately after the description of the rotation values.

(reached character limit…)

(…continued)

* Please remove "(the center horizontal row)" to avoid repeating the definition of the diagnostic bus.

* Some concepts are repeated unnecessarily and could be removed.

  • The first paragraph states that strips rotate "in multiples of 90°", which is already explained later by the definition of the rotation values.

  • The interpretation of the routing rules repeats the definition of an Open Channel, which has already been given when introducing the three states.

* The example could be expanded to show a complete rotation cycle (e.g. +1 +2 -1), illustrating both clockwise and counter-clockwise rotations as well as the concept of multiple rotations per round, and making the cumulative effect of the rotations easier to follow.

* Consider using a smaller example (e.g. a 5 x 7 matrix instead of 7 x 9). A more compact example would be easier to read while still demonstrating the same mechanics.

* Please remove the annotation "(reversed)" from the example. It hints at the rotation behaviour instead of explaining it.

* Please explain how each output is obtained by explicitly showing the states of both strips and how they overlap.

Output
* Please add "<<[[n]] Lines>>:" at the beginning.

* Please remove "(the center horizontal row)" to avoid repeating the definition of the diagnostic bus.

Constraints
* Please remove all the constraints.

* Please add a constraint for each of h, w, n and (each integer in) turns.

Stub generator
* Please rewrite Line 4 using loopline of "word" instead of "int" or "string".

Tags
* Please remove "Graphs" and "Geometry".

Cases
* The first case pair should be a simple introductory example, similar to the one in the statement, i.e. all positions outside the two strips are Open Channels.

* Test 4: w is 24, not 25.

* Each test-validator pair should avoid mixing cases where [[h]] > [[w]] and [[h]] < [[w]].

* Please add a pair of cases where [[h]] = [[w]].

* I'll provide more feedback on the cases after the above points have been addressed. I've also noted that you'll refine them later on.

Thanks.

That's a lot 😵‍💫. It looks like I've made quite a mess of the statement. I'll take some time to go through all of these points carefully.

Thanks again for the thorough review.
